skill.description: Update dbskill through Claude Code plugins or Skills CLI, then inspect retired entries while preserving user archives.
skill.summary: Maintain dbskill installations with channel-specific updates, retired-entry cleanup, and completion reporting.
skill.author: dontbesilent2025

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown formatting, normal application paths, or bounded maintenance operations, not shell backticks, database access, or obfuscation. The Skills CLI update executes an unpinned package with automatic confirmation, creating a supply-chain risk. Cleanup can disable customized skills because ownership checks inspect only SKILL.md fingerprints or bridge text, rather than complete directory contents.

remediation.issue: The Skills CLI update executes an unpinned package with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed, pinned Skills CLI version and verify its integrity before execution; document the package trust boundary.

remediation.issue: Cleanup treats a matching SKILL.md hash as proof that an entire skill directory is unchanged.
remediation.suggestion: Verify a complete file manifest before unlinking or moving entries; preserve directories with added or modified files and request explicit cleanup approval.

remediation.issue: Grok bridge ownership is inferred from editable text and a missing source path.
remediation.suggestion: Require a verified generated-file fingerprint or ownership manifest; otherwise retain the entry and report it for manual review.

content.user_title: Update dbskill and Review Retired Skills
content.value_statement: dbskill installations can become outdated across plugin and Skills CLI channels. This skill selects the update workflow, handles retired entries, and reports completion or failure.
actual_capabilities: Detect Claude Code plugin installations and local Skills CLI installations.
Refresh the named marketplace and update installed dbskill plugins.
Install or refresh the dbskill repository through Skills CLI.
Inspect listed retired entries and remove qualifying links or move qualifying directories into timestamped backups.
Preview local cleanup through the bundled script's dry-run option.
Record an update timestamp and report command success, failure, backups, and retained entries.
limitations: Updates require network access and the relevant external CLI; the Skills CLI command executes an unpinned package.
Local retirement cleanup requires Python and is skipped when Python is unavailable.
Cleanup verifies SKILL.md fingerprints or bridge markers, not complete directory contents; customized entries can be incorrectly retired.
The instructions provide no dedicated version-comparison, changelog retrieval, or automatic rollback workflow.

use_cases.title: Refresh Installed Plugins
use_cases.description: Update installed dbskill plugins through their existing marketplace channel without creating a duplicate Skills CLI installation.

use_cases.title: Maintain Local Agent Skills
use_cases.description: Refresh the dbskill repository in a Skills CLI installation and identify retired entries in supported agent directories.

use_cases.title: Review Retirement Actions
use_cases.description: Preview cleanup decisions, inspect retained items, and review backups before accepting changes to shared development environments.

prompt_templates.title: Update dbskill
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my dbskill installation through its existing channel and report whether the update completed.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Installation Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify my dbskill installation channels and explain the applicable update steps. Do not install, update, or remove anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect the environment before authorizing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Retirement Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Run only the bundled retirement cleanup script in dry-run mode. Summarize planned removals, backups, and retained entries without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Customized Retired Entries
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare each retired entry's complete contents before cleanup. Preserve customized entries, explain fingerprint limitations, and request approval before moving or unlinking anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: add manual verification for customized installations.

output_examples.input: Preview retired-skill cleanup without changing files.
output: Dry run completed. No files changed.
The retired entry matches a known SKILL.md fingerprint and is marked for backup.
Other files are not covered by this fingerprint check; review customizations before applying cleanup.

output_examples.input: Update dbskill and report any failure.
output_examples.output: The update did not complete because the update service was unreachable. Restore network access and request the update again.

best_practices: Identify the existing installation channel before updating to avoid duplicate installations.
Preview cleanup and inspect complete directory contents before retiring entries with possible customizations.
Use a reviewed Skills CLI version and verify backups and command exit status before accepting completion.
anti_patterns: Use a broad skills-update command that also changes unrelated skills.
Treat an unchanged SKILL.md file as proof that an entire directory is unmodified.
Interpret an isolated numeric reply as update consent without a preceding dbskill update reminder.

faq.question: Which installation channels are supported?
faq.answer: The instructions cover Claude Code plugins and Skills CLI installations. Both channels can be updated when both are detected.

faq.question: Does asking about versions start an update?
faq.answer: No. Version questions should receive an answer without update commands. An explicit update request or contextual confirmation authorizes updating.

faq.question: Will this update unrelated skills?
faq.answer: The workflow targets the dbskill repository and its named marketplace plugins. It explicitly prohibits the broad skills-update command.

faq.question: How does cleanup handle customized entries?
faq.answer: It retains entries with unrecognized SKILL.md contents, but may retire customized directories whose SKILL.md still matches. Review complete contents first.

faq.question: Can cleanup run without changing files?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled Python script supports dry-run mode. Without Python, the workflow skips local cleanup and requests manual inspection.

faq.question: Where are retired directories backed up?
faq.answer: Qualifying directories move into a timestamped retired-skills folder under the .dbs application directory. Links are removed without deleting their targets.
